med_tabii.title: Madd Tabii (Natural Elongation)
med_tabii.rule: When a madd letter is not followed by a cause of elongation (hamza or sukun), it is lengthened by one alif (two counts).

0.explanation: The letter alif carries the elongation.

1.explanation: The letter waw carries the elongation.

idgam_meal_gunne.title: Idgham Ma'al Ghunnah
idgam_meal_gunne.rule: When noon sakinah or tanween is followed by one of the letters ي ن م و, the sounds merge with ghunnah.

0.explanation: The noon meets ya, so idgham occurs.

1.explanation: The noon meets meem, so idgham occurs.

idgam-bila-gunne.title: Idgham Bila Ghunnah
idgam-bila-gunne.rule: When noon sakinah or tanween is followed by lam (ل) or ra (ر), the sounds merge without ghunnah.

0.explanation: The noon meets ra, so idgham without ghunnah occurs.

1.explanation: The tanween meets lam, so idgham without ghunnah occurs.

ihfa.title: Ikhfa
ihfa.rule: When noon sakinah or tanween is followed by an ikhfa letter, the noon sound is concealed and voiced through the nose.

0.explanation: The noon sakinah meets za, so ikhfa occurs.

1.explanation: The noon sakinah meets shin, so ikhfa occurs.

izhar.title: Izhar
izhar.rule: When noon sakinah or tanween is followed by a throat letter, the noon is pronounced clearly.

0.explanation: The noon sakinah meets kha, so izhar occurs.

1.explanation: The tanween meets alif (hamza), so izhar occurs.

iklab.title: Iqlab
iklab.rule: When noon sakinah or tanween is followed by ba (ب), the noon sound turns into meem and is read with ghunnah.

0.explanation: The noon sakinah meets ba, so it turns into a meem sound.

1.explanation: The tanween meets ba, so it turns into a meem sound.

kalkale.title: Qalqalah
kalkale.rule: When one of the qalqalah letters (ق ط ب ج د) has sukun, it is pronounced with a strong, bouncing sound at its point of articulation.

0.explanation: When stopping (waqf), qaf is read with sukun, so qalqalah occurs.

1.explanation: Dal has sukun, so qalqalah occurs.

ra_hukmu.title: Rules of Ra
ra_hukmu.desc: How the letter ra is pronounced
ra_hukmu.rule: Ra with fatha or damma is read heavy; with kasra it is read light. With sukun, the vowel of the preceding letter decides.

0.explanation: Ra has fatha, so it is read heavy.

med_muttasil.title: Madd Muttasil (Connected Elongation)
med_muttasil.rule: When a hamza follows a madd letter in the same word, it is Madd Muttasil and is lengthened more.

0.explanation: Alif and hamza are in the same word, so it is lengthened more.
